turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not threatened by you, Sandip. I am merely stating the facts, as I am bound to do by my duty as a zamindar.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, do the facts you speak of truly reflect the reality of our tenantry's situation, or are they a part of the information you have come to share?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Why, Nikhil, you're as transparent as a lotus leaf on the surface of a stagnant pond. I know exactly why you're here, and it's not out of a sudden concern for my tenantry's welfare.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your frivolous accusations, Sandip. As a zamindar, I am bound to protect the interests of my people.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I must admit, Nikhil, that your words have piqued my interest. Can you provide more insight into the nature of these potential attacks, and how they might affect my husband's estate?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Bimala, always the voice of reason in a household of ruffians and scoundrels. Nikhil, I suppose you're trying to scare me into submission, but I'm afraid your threats are about as effective as a rusty blade against a well-fed tiger.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your flippant remarks, Sandip. My warnings are based on concrete evidence and a deep understanding of the situation. I implore you to take them seriously and take necessary precautions to protect your estate.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I sense that there's more to this situation than mere threats and warnings. Can you tell me more about the underlying reasons for these potential attacks?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, I'm surprised you'd stoop to spreading unsubstantiated rumors about my estate. Perhaps you're trying to deflect attention from your own mismanagement of the neighboring estates.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, I will not stand for your continued dismissal of my warnings. It is time for you to take responsibility for the security of your estate, rather than relying on my benevolence to protect you from harm.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I believe it would be helpful to know more about the economic factors at play here. Are there any specific changes or decisions that have led to this potential tension with the local Mussulmans?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, please, spare me the theatrics. I'm not buying into your doomsday scenario, and I'm certainly not going to cower in fear just because you've declared my estate a potential target.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, I warn you once more: do not underestimate the situation. The local Mussulmans are growing increasingly resentful of your actions, and it is only a matter of time before they take drastic measures.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I see that you've been making efforts to modernize the neighboring estates. Could you elaborate on the specific innovations you've introduced, and how they might be contributing to the current tensions?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always so full of dire predictions and warnings. I'm starting to think you're more concerned with being right than with actually helping me, don't you?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, I have no interest in being right, only in being prepared. The situation is not a matter of prediction, but of fact. Your actions have consequences, and I will not stand idly by while you ignore the warnings.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I've been paying attention to the changes in the neighboring estates, and I must admit that I find the modernization efforts intriguing. Could you explain how you've adapted the traditional farming practices to improve yields without disrupting the local economy?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Bimala, always so fascinated by the intricacies of modernization, but do you ever stop to consider the beauty of the old ways? I swear, the only thing Nikhil's innovations have modernized is his sense of self-importance.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not engage in a debate about the merits of modernization, Sandip. The fact remains that the local Mussulmans have been making overtures towards me, and I will not stand idly by while our estates are threatened.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I've been considering the local Mussulmans' concerns, Nikhil. What do you believe is the root cause of their dissatisfaction with our estate?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
